raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What

Add `mamba` as a selective activation-recompute target. With `--recompute-granularity selective --recompute-modules '[mamba]'`, `MambaLayer` checkpoints the mixer (convolution plus selective SSM/SSD compute) instead of retaining its activations.

## Why

In Mamba-hybrid models the mixer activations can be a material part of long-sequence memory. Megatron already lets selective recompute target attention, MLP, MoE, and several GDN components, but not Mamba, leaving full-layer recompute as the only way to trade compute for this activation memory.

## Implementation

- Add `mamba` to the `recompute_modules` validation and documentation.
- Warn when `mamba` is selected with `moe_shortcut_connection`: shortcut MoE uses two-stage mixer execution and does not enter this checkpoint path.
- Use `tensor_parallel.checkpoint` for BF16/FP16/FP32.
- Use Transformer Engine checkpointing for FP8/FP4 so recomputation does not update amax/scaling history twice.
- Preserve `inference_context` and `packed_seq_params` through both paths.
- Keep eval and inference on the direct mixer path.
- Bypass activation checkpointing during local CUDA-graph warmup/capture, matching the existing tensor-parallel checkpoint contract and avoiding TE checkpoint's `.grad()` incompatibility.

The option is default-off and does not change existing runs unless `mamba` is explicitly selected.

## Tests

The focused suite retains the 12 routing/bypass cases and adds three shortcut-MoE warning cases. Six new tests build a real `HybridModel` with `MambaMixer`, compare recompute-off versus selective logits and all parameter gradients, and verify that the mixer runs again during backward. The matrix covers TP1, TP2, TP2 with sequence parallelism, and both memory-efficient and explicit Mamba paths. The mixer and checkpoint functions are not mocked in these model tests.

On the preceding head `6f88cf61288a`, NVIDIA CI passed the focused suite and H100 integration jobs; the SSM bucket passed 387 tests with 9 skips. Those results do not cover the new tests.

For the October 5 review update, Black, isort, Ruff, Pylint, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` pass. The repository formatter script exits successfully; its non-blocking mypy step still reports missing dependencies/stubs and an existing `normalization` override type error. The local macOS pytest attempt stopped during normal Core import because Triton is unavailable; no test cases ran. Linux CPU and CUDA validation of the new cases remain pending, and CI needs authorization for the updated head.

An earlier 8×B200 run covered packed BF16 and FP8 training plus local Mamba CUDA-graph capture/replay. At sequence length 16K (CP1/DP8), selective and full FP8 recompute both completed without NaNs or OOMs and differed by about `1e-5` relative loss. A 20-step BF16 selective/full comparison had a maximum absolute difference of `2.37e-3`; repeating selective with the same seed produced `2.24e-3` run-to-run variation, so the cross-mode difference was within the measured baseline nondeterminism.

At the 24K BF16 boundary with the same model/topology, no recompute OOMed before completing its first step, while selective Mamba recompute completed both steps without NaNs (`10.58632 → 10.09310`) with rank-0 peak allocated memory of 96.13 GiB and 102.09 GiB. At 32K both modes OOMed before a complete step. Because the failed baseline has no common completed step, this is capacity evidence rather than a like-for-like percentage-memory comparison.

The intended CP8 matrix could not run because this environment did not expose a compatible deterministic attention backend, so these results are explicitly CP1/DP8 rather than CP8. Raw numbers and the CUDA-graph baseline comparison are in the PR discussion.
Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex

Strict Review Summary — Findings by severity: CRITICAL: 0 · IMPORTANT: 1 · SUGGESTION: 0.

The change is small, follows the established selective-recompute pattern, correctly gates to training-only (self.training and inference_context is None, so the stateful SSM update is never re-executed in inference), and tensor_parallel.checkpoint already bypasses recomputation during CUDA-graph warmup/capture (random.py:647). The config allow-list, docstring, and validation updates are consistent. The mandatory unused-identifier check passes: recompute_mamba_mixer is read in forward, and the new functools/tensor_parallel imports are both used.

Most impactful finding — [IMPORTANT] fp8/fp4 recompute path: The Mamba mixer runs fp8/fp4 GEMMs (in_proj/out_proj are TE linear modules; mamba_mixer.py:227 has an explicit fp8 assertion), but the new code unconditionally uses tensor_parallel.checkpoint. The established selective-recompute pattern (transformer_layer.py:824-842) branches on config.fp8 or config.fp4 and routes through te_checkpoint, which enters TE activation-recompute phase so fp8 amax/scaling state is not double-updated during the backward-pass recompute. Without this branch, fp8 Mamba-hybrid training re-runs the mixer fp8 GEMMs under a plain enable_grad context, double-updating amax history and silently corrupting fp8 scaling — invisible at bf16, harmful under fp8. Recommend mirroring the transformer-layer fp8 branch.

Risk assessment — Low-to-moderate. For the common bf16/CP long-context case this is a clean, well-scoped memory/speed trade-off and is a no-op unless "mamba" is explicitly added to recompute_modules (fully backward compatible). The one gap is fp8/fp4, where fp8-scaling correctness is at risk. As the PR notes, it is still a draft pending convergence/loss-parity and peak-memory validation vs full recompute — that validation should include an fp8 run to exercise the path above.

@Phlip79 Thanks for the quick vetting and the strict review. The fp8/fp4 finding is addressed in 20eeb77 (mirrors the `te_checkpoint` branch from `transformer_layer.py`). Could you `/ok to test 20eeb77` so CI runs on the updated SHA?

@Phlip79 following up on my Jul 10 comment — the fp8/fp4 gating your strict-review flagged is fixed in 20eeb77, and that SHA is still waiting on `/ok to test` (only DCO and check-approval have run). Could you authorize CI on it so this can move to review?

@Phlip79 rebased this onto current main as 4811efa0a01cb7f0b6f5d1e3081a902298199be5. The FP8/FP4 TE path from your earlier review is preserved, and the refreshed branch also handles local CUDA-graph warmup/capture explicitly; without that bypass, TE checkpoint can fail on the graph builder’s `.grad()` path. The focused suite now has 11 passing routing/bypass cases and the 8×B200 matrix is in progress. Could you review this SHA and run `/ok to test 4811efa0a01cb7f0b6f5d1e3081a902298199be5`?

Finished the 8×B200 pass on `4811efa`.

The focused recompute suite is 11/11. For packed CP1/DP8 training at seq 16K, BF16 selective and full both completed 20 steps with no NaNs or OOMs. Their max absolute loss difference was `2.37e-3`; a same-seed selective repeat differed from the first selective run by `2.24e-3`, so the selective/full delta is within the run-to-run variation measured on this setup.

FP8 selective and full also completed cleanly. The two losses were `10.58814, 10.52099` for selective and `10.58803, 10.52089` for full (roughly `1e-5` relative difference). Rank-0 peak allocated memory was 66.26 GB for selective and 30.90 GB for full. In BF16, selective reached 67.30 GB and full 30.65 GB by the second step; the no-recompute two-step baseline was about 71.4 GB.

I also ran FP8 selective recompute with local Mamba CUDA graphs. The non-packed case built 40 graphs and completed 4/4 steps; the post-capture steps ran in about 136 ms and 128 ms, so replay was exercised rather than only capture. The packed case built the same 40 graphs but failed the first runner lookup. The identical failure reproduces with recompute disabled, so that is a packed/dynamic-runner baseline limitation in this configuration, not selective recompute behavior.

The intended CP8 run was blocked because this container had no compatible deterministic attention backend for CP8. I am reporting the topology explicitly rather than presenting the CP1/DP8 fallback as CP8 evidence.

One useful boundary point to add: with the same packed BF16 CP1/DP8 setup at sequence length 24K, the no-recompute run OOMed before completing its first step, while selective Mamba recompute completed both steps with no NaNs (`10.58632 → 10.09310`). Rank-0 peak allocated memory was 96.13 GiB on step 1 and 102.09 GiB on step 2.

At 32K both modes OOMed before a complete step. Since the 24K baseline has no completed step, I am treating this as evidence that selective recompute extends the trainable sequence-length boundary, not as a like-for-like percentage-memory comparison.

Re-ran the focused recompute suite on current head `caee7ca7fecf68b5b086953209a3f902dc3ed5f2` with 8 ranks:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_mamba_recompute.py
```

Each rank executed all 12 cases: 12 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed (96 passes total). This covers packed-sequence metadata forwarding and the FP8/FP4 recompute routing, and the worktree was clean.

This is unit-level validation only; I am still keeping the separate production Mamba forward/backward off-vs-selective gradient parity run as a distinct follow-up rather than treating these unit results as that evidence. Could you `/ok to test caee7ca7fecf68b5b086953209a3f902dc3ed5f2` so CI can run on the current head?

@Phlip79, could you revisit this selective Mamba recompute PR? The earlier FP8/FP4 routing concern has been addressed, and the follow-up comments document both targeted tests and the separate production forward/backward parity check. Could you review the current diff or route it to the appropriate owner, and authorize CI if appropriate? Thanks.

@jiemingz Rebased at `ebe20fd8041`, preserving the new two-stage Mamba methods and the selective-recompute helper. Local lint checks pass; GPU parity and the two-stage/recompute combination still need validation on this head. Could you review the integration and authorize CI?

Of course, if you'd like to add recompute support for the combination with shortcut MoE, that'd even be preferrable to just adding a warning.

@janEbert Added the warning in `TransformerConfig.__post_init__` and three cases checking when it appears.

The new real-model tests build `HybridModel` with `MambaMixer` and compare recompute-off/selective logits and every parameter gradient. A forward hook also checks that the actual mixer runs again during backward. They cover TP1, TP2, sequence parallelism, and both Mamba kernel paths, without mocking the mixer or checkpoint.

I’ve left shortcut MoE unsupported here: it calls the split pre/core and post-core methods, so checkpointing the ordinary mixer forward would not cover that execution path. Adding support needs a separate checkpoint boundary around the split path.

The update is at `2f9dc4dbc`. Formatting and static checks pass. The local macOS pytest attempt stopped at the missing Triton import before running any tests; Linux/CUDA results for the new cases are still pending. Could you authorize CI with `/ok to test 2f9dc4dbc`?
/ok to test 414aed8904680760ba20d594f11add499da5ba90
@janEbert The CI run for `414aed890` has been waiting at `cicd-wait-in-queue` since October 6. Could you check what is holding the `test` environment gate?

**[IMPORTANT Implementation]** This recompute path unconditionally uses `tensor_parallel.checkpoint`, but the Mamba mixer runs fp8/fp4 GEMMs — `in_proj`/`out_proj` are `TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear`/`TERowParallelLinear`, and `mamba_mixer.py:227` has an explicit fp8 assertion. The established selective-recompute pattern in `transformer_layer.py:824-842` branches on fp8:

```python
if self.config.fp8 or self.config.fp4:
    from megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine import te_checkpoint
    mlp_output_with_bias = te_checkpoint(apply_module(self.mlp), False,
        tensor_parallel.random.get_cuda_rng_tracker, self.pg_collection.tp, ...)
else:
    mlp_output_with_bias = tensor_parallel.checkpoint(...)
```

**Why it matters:** the plain `CheckpointFunction` (random.py:614-621) re-runs the forward under `torch.enable_grad()` in backward with no fp8-recompute context. TE's `te_checkpoint` sets the `activation_recompute` phase so the fp8 amax history / delayed-scaling factors are not updated a second time during recompute. Without it, fp8 mamba training will double-update amax and silently corrupt fp8 scaling, degrading convergence — while looking fine at bf16.

**Fix:** mirror the transformer-layer branch and route through `te_checkpoint` (passing `self.mixer`'s pg_collection TP group) when `self.config.fp8 or self.config.fp4`. Note the mixer is constructed with its own `pg_collection`, so you'll need the TP group available on the layer/mixer.

+from megatron.core.transformer import TransformerConfig, cuda_graphs
+from megatron.core.transformer.identity_op import IdentityFuncOp, IdentityOp
+
+_TP_GROUP = object()
+_INFERENCE_CONTEXT = object()
+_PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS = object()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.internal
+class TestMambaModelRecompute:
+    """Compare real Mamba kernels and parameter gradients with checkpointing enabled."""
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("use_mem_eff_path", [True, False])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_size,sequence_parallel", [(1, False), (2, False), (2, True)])
+    def test_forward_backward_parity(self, tp_size, sequence_parallel, use_mem_eff_path):
+        from megatron.core.models.hybrid.hybrid_layer_specs import hybrid_stack_spec
+        from megatron.core.models.hybrid.hybrid_model import HybridModel
+        from megatron.core.ssm.mamba_mixer import MambaMixer
+        from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed
+        from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(tp_size, 1)
+        try:
+            model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+            pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+
+            def build_model(recompute):
+                config = TransformerConfig(
+                    hidden_size=256,
+                    num_layers=1,
+                    num_attention_heads=4,
+                    tensor_model_parallel_size=tp_size,
+                    sequence_parallel=sequence_parallel,
+                    use_cpu_initialization=True,
+                    use_mamba_mem_eff_path=use_mem_eff_path,
+                    hidden_dropout=0.0,
+                    attention_dropout=0.0,
+                    recompute_granularity="selective" if recompute else None,
+                    recompute_modules=["mamba"],
+                )
+                return (
+                    HybridModel(
+                        config,
+                        hybrid_stack_spec,
+                        vocab_size=128,
+                        max_sequence_length=32,
+                        hybrid_layer_pattern="M",
+                        parallel_output=False,
+                        pg_collection=pg_collection,
+                    )
+                    .cuda()
+                    .train()
+                )
+
+            baseline = build_model(False)
+            recomputed = build_model(True)
+            recomputed.load_state_dict(baseline.state_dict())
+            mixer = recomputed.decoder.layers[0].mixer
+            assert isinstance(mixer, MambaMixer)
+            mixer_grad_modes = []
+            hook = mixer.register_forward_hook(
+                lambda _module, _inputs, _output: mixer_grad_modes.append(torch.is_grad_enabled())
+            )
+            input_ids = torch.arange(64, device="cuda").reshape(2, 32)
+            position_ids = torch.arange(32, device="cuda").expand(2, -1)
+            baseline_logits = baseline(input_ids, position_ids, attention_mask=None)
+            recomputed_logits = recomputed(input_ids, position_ids, attention_mask=None)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(recomputed_logits, baseline_logits, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            baseline_logits.float().square().mean().backward()
+            recomputed_logits.float().square().mean().backward()
+            hook.remove()
+            assert mixer_grad_modes == [False, True], "The real mixer must run again in backward."
+
+            baseline_parameters = dict(baseline.named_parameters())
+            for name, parameter in recomputed.named_parameters():
+                reference_gradient = baseline_parameters[name].grad
+                assert parameter.grad is not None, f"Missing recomputed gradient: {name}"
+                assert reference_gradient is not None, f"Missing baseline gradient: {name}"
+                assert torch.isfinite(parameter.grad).all(), f"Non-finite gradient: {name}"
+                torch.testing.assert_close(parameter.grad, reference_gradient, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)
+        finally:
+            Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rank", [0, 1])
+def test_mamba_recompute_warns_with_shortcut_moe(caplog, monkeypatch, rank):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(_rank_utils, "safe_get_rank", lambda: rank)
+    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger="megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config"):
+        TransformerConfig(
+            hidden_size=256,
+            num_layers=2,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            num_moe_experts=8,
+            moe_shortcut_connection=True,
+            recompute_granularity="selective",
+            recompute_modules=["mamba"],
+        )
+    warnings = [r for r in caplog.records if "Mamba mixer recomputation" in r.message]
+    assert len(warnings) == int(rank in _rank_utils.get_default_log_ranks())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("shortcut_moe", "modules"), [(False, ["mamba"]), (True, ["layernorm"])])
+def test_mamba_recompute_warning_only_for_shortcut_moe(caplog, shortcut_moe, modules):
+    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger="megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config"):
+        TransformerConfig(
+            hidden_size=256,
+            num_layers=2,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            num_moe_experts=8,
+            moe_shortcut_connection=shortcut_moe,

+            recompute_modules=modules,
+        )
+    assert not any("Mamba mixer recomputation" in r.message for r in caplog.records)

+class _RecordingMixer(torch.nn.Module):
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        hidden_states,
+        inference_context=None,
+        packed_seq_params=None,
+        packed_sequence_cp_metadata=None,
+    ):
+        self.calls.append(
+            (hidden_states, inference_context, packed_seq_params, packed_sequence_cp_metadata)
+        )
+        return hidden_states + 1, None
+
+
+def _build_test_layer(recompute_granularity, recompute_modules, *, fp8=False, fp4=False):
+    config = TransformerConfig(
+        hidden_size=8,
+        num_layers=1,
+        num_attention_heads=1,
+        recompute_granularity=recompute_granularity,
+        recompute_modules=recompute_modules,
+        use_cpu_initialization=True,
+    )
+    config.fp8 = fp8
+    config.fp4 = fp4
+    return MambaLayer(
+        config,
+        MambaLayerSubmodules(norm=IdentityOp, mixer=_RecordingMixer, mamba_bda=IdentityFuncOp),
+        pg_collection=ProcessGroupCollection(tp=_TP_GROUP),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("granularity", "modules", "training", "inference_context", "fp8"),
+    [
+        pytest.param(None, ["mamba"], True, None, False, id="recompute-disabled"),
+        pytest.param("selective", ["core_attn"], True, None, False, id="mamba-not-selected"),
+        pytest.param("selective", ["mamba"], False, None, False, id="eval"),
+        pytest.param("selective", ["mamba"], True, _INFERENCE_CONTEXT, True, id="inference"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_mamba_mixer_bypasses_checkpoint(
+    monkeypatch, granularity, modules, training, inference_context, fp8
+):
+    def unexpected_checkpoint(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("checkpoint should not run")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(tensor_parallel, "checkpoint", unexpected_checkpoint)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(transformer_engine, "te_checkpoint", unexpected_checkpoint)
+    layer = _build_test_layer(granularity, modules, fp8=fp8)
+    layer.train(training)
+    hidden_states = torch.ones(2, 1, layer.config.hidden_size)
+
+    result = layer._run_mamba_mixer(hidden_states, inference_context, _PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS)
+
+    assert torch.equal(result[0], hidden_states + 1)
+    call = layer.mixer.calls[0]
+    assert call[0] is hidden_states
+    assert call[1:] == (inference_context, _PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS, None)
+
+
+def test_mamba_mixer_uses_tensor_parallel_checkpoint(monkeypatch):
+    checkpoint_call = {}
+
+    def checkpoint(forward_func, distribute_saved_activations, *args):
+        checkpoint_call.update(distribute=distribute_saved_activations, args=args)
+        return forward_func(*args)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(tensor_parallel, "checkpoint", checkpoint)
+    layer = _build_test_layer("selective", ["mamba"])
+    hidden_states = torch.ones(2, 1, layer.config.hidden_size)
+
+    result = layer._run_mamba_mixer(hidden_states, None, _PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS)
+
+    assert torch.equal(result[0], hidden_states + 1)
+    assert checkpoint_call["distribute"] is False
+    assert checkpoint_call["args"] == (hidden_states,)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("fp8", "fp4"), [pytest.param(True, False, id="fp8"), pytest.param(False, True, id="fp4")]
+)
+def test_mamba_mixer_uses_te_checkpoint_for_quantized_recompute(monkeypatch, fp8, fp4):
+    checkpoint_call = {}
+
+    def te_checkpoint(forward_func, distribute, get_rng_state_tracker, tp_group, *args, **kwargs):
+        checkpoint_call.update(
+            distribute=distribute,
+            get_rng_state_tracker=get_rng_state_tracker,
+            tp_group=tp_group,
+            args=args,
+            kwargs=kwargs,
+        )
+        return forward_func(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(transformer_engine, "te_checkpoint", te_checkpoint)
+    layer = _build_test_layer("selective", ["mamba"], fp8=fp8, fp4=fp4)
+    hidden_states = torch.ones(2, 1, layer.config.hidden_size)
+
+    result = layer._run_mamba_mixer(hidden_states, None, _PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS)
+
+    assert torch.equal(result[0], hidden_states + 1)
+    assert checkpoint_call["distribute"] is False
+    assert checkpoint_call["get_rng_state_tracker"] is tensor_parallel.random.get_cuda_rng_tracker
+    assert checkpoint_call["tp_group"] is _TP_GROUP
+    assert checkpoint_call["args"] == (hidden_states,)
+    assert checkpoint_call["kwargs"] == {
+        "inference_context": None,
+        "packed_seq_params": _PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS,
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("fp8", "fp4"), [pytest.param(True, False, id="fp8"), pytest.param(False, True, id="fp4")]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("graph_state", ["warmup", "capture"])
+def test_quantized_mamba_mixer_bypasses_checkpoint_during_cuda_graph(
+    monkeypatch, fp8, fp4, graph_state
+):
+    def unexpected_checkpoint(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("checkpoint should not run during CUDA graph warmup or capture")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(tensor_parallel, "checkpoint", unexpected_checkpoint)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(transformer_engine, "te_checkpoint", unexpected_checkpoint)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cuda_graphs, "is_graph_warmup", lambda: graph_state == "warmup")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cuda_graphs, "is_graph_capturing", lambda: graph_state == "capture")
+    layer = _build_test_layer("selective", ["mamba"], fp8=fp8, fp4=fp4)
+    hidden_states = torch.ones(2, 1, layer.config.hidden_size)
+
+    result = layer._run_mamba_mixer(hidden_states, None, _PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS)
+
+    assert torch.equal(result[0], hidden_states + 1)
+    call = layer.mixer.calls[0]
+    assert call[0] is hidden_states
+    assert call[1:] == (None, _PACKED_SEQ_PARAMS, None)
+
+
+def test_mamba_mixer_forwards_packed_sequence_cp_metadata(monkeypatch):
+    def checkpoint(forward_func, distribute_saved_activations, *args):
+        return forward_func(*args)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(tensor_parallel, "checkpoint", checkpoint)
+    layer = _build_test_layer("selective", ["mamba"])

**[IMPORTANT Implementation]** This recompute path unconditionally uses `tensor_parallel.checkpoint`, but the Mamba mixer runs fp8/fp4 GEMMs — `in_proj`/`out_proj` are `TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear`/`TERowParallelLinear`, and `mamba_mixer.py:227` has an explicit fp8 assertion. The established selective-recompute pattern in `transformer_layer.py:824-842` branches on fp8:

```python
if self.config.fp8 or self.config.fp4:
    from megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine import te_checkpoint
    mlp_output_with_bias = te_checkpoint(apply_module(self.mlp), False,
        tensor_parallel.random.get_cuda_rng_tracker, self.pg_collection.tp, ...)
else:
    mlp_output_with_bias = tensor_parallel.checkpoint(...)
```

**Why it matters:** the plain `CheckpointFunction` (random.py:614-621) re-runs the forward under `torch.enable_grad()` in backward with no fp8-recompute context. TE's `te_checkpoint` sets the `activation_recompute` phase so the fp8 amax history / delayed-scaling factors are not updated a second time during recompute. Without it, fp8 mamba training will double-update amax and silently corrupt fp8 scaling, degrading convergence — while looking fine at bf16.

**Fix:** mirror the transformer-layer branch and route through `te_checkpoint` (passing `self.mixer`'s pg_collection TP group) when `self.config.fp8 or self.config.fp4`. Note the mixer is constructed with its own `pg_collection`, so you'll need the TP group available on the layer/mixer.

Strict Review Summary — Findings by severity: CRITICAL: 0 · IMPORTANT: 1 · SUGGESTION: 0.

The change is small, follows the established selective-recompute pattern, correctly gates to training-only (self.training and inference_context is None, so the stateful SSM update is never re-executed in inference), and tensor_parallel.checkpoint already bypasses recomputation during CUDA-graph warmup/capture (random.py:647). The config allow-list, docstring, and validation updates are consistent. The mandatory unused-identifier check passes: recompute_mamba_mixer is read in forward, and the new functools/tensor_parallel imports are both used.

Most impactful finding — [IMPORTANT] fp8/fp4 recompute path: The Mamba mixer runs fp8/fp4 GEMMs (in_proj/out_proj are TE linear modules; mamba_mixer.py:227 has an explicit fp8 assertion), but the new code unconditionally uses tensor_parallel.checkpoint. The established selective-recompute pattern (transformer_layer.py:824-842) branches on config.fp8 or config.fp4 and routes through te_checkpoint, which enters TE activation-recompute phase so fp8 amax/scaling state is not double-updated during the backward-pass recompute. Without this branch, fp8 Mamba-hybrid training re-runs the mixer fp8 GEMMs under a plain enable_grad context, double-updating amax history and silently corrupting fp8 scaling — invisible at bf16, harmful under fp8. Recommend mirroring the transformer-layer fp8 branch.

Risk assessment — Low-to-moderate. For the common bf16/CP long-context case this is a clean, well-scoped memory/speed trade-off and is a no-op unless "mamba" is explicitly added to recompute_modules (fully backward compatible). The one gap is fp8/fp4, where fp8-scaling correctness is at risk. As the PR notes, it is still a draft pending convergence/loss-parity and peak-memory validation vs full recompute — that validation should include an fp8 run to exercise the path above.

The focused recompute suite is 11/11. For packed CP1/DP8 training at seq 16K, BF16 selective and full both completed 20 steps with no NaNs or OOMs. Their max absolute loss difference was `2.37e-3`; a same-seed selective repeat differed from the first selective run by `2.24e-3`, so the selective/full delta is within the run-to-run variation measured on this setup.

FP8 selective and full also completed cleanly. The two losses were `10.58814, 10.52099` for selective and `10.58803, 10.52089` for full (roughly `1e-5` relative difference). Rank-0 peak allocated memory was 66.26 GB for selective and 30.90 GB for full. In BF16, selective reached 67.30 GB and full 30.65 GB by the second step; the no-recompute two-step baseline was about 71.4 GB.

I also ran FP8 selective recompute with local Mamba CUDA graphs. The non-packed case built 40 graphs and completed 4/4 steps; the post-capture steps ran in about 136 ms and 128 ms, so replay was exercised rather than only capture. The packed case built the same 40 graphs but failed the first runner lookup. The identical failure reproduces with recompute disabled, so that is a packed/dynamic-runner baseline limitation in this configuration, not selective recompute behavior.

The intended CP8 run was blocked because this container had no compatible deterministic attention backend for CP8. I am reporting the topology explicitly rather than presenting the CP1/DP8 fallback as CP8 evidence.

One useful boundary point to add: with the same packed BF16 CP1/DP8 setup at sequence length 24K, the no-recompute run OOMed before completing its first step, while selective Mamba recompute completed both steps with no NaNs (`10.58632 → 10.09310`). Rank-0 peak allocated memory was 96.13 GiB on step 1 and 102.09 GiB on step 2.

At 32K both modes OOMed before a complete step. Since the 24K baseline has no completed step, I am treating this as evidence that selective recompute extends the trainable sequence-length boundary, not as a like-for-like percentage-memory comparison.
